election._note: Closed-list national PR (D'Hondt) with a 5% threshold for parties and 7% for blocs, back from the 2019 mixed system. Elected 28 September 2025, so the next is due by autumn 2029. Electoral Code of Moldova; Wikipedia, '2025 Moldovan parliamentary election'.

dissolution._note: The President may dissolve Parliament only if no government is invested within 45 days after two requests, or if it is blocked for three months (Art. 85) -- the template's confidence_failure reads the government-formation trigger. Constitution of Moldova, Art. 85.

head_of_state._note: The President, directly elected for four years since 2016 (two terms at most); re-elected in the November 2024 run-off, so the next falls in autumn 2028. Constitution of Moldova, Arts. 78, 80.
head_of_state.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 143: two thirds of the deputies, six months after the initiative; the provisions on sovereignty, independence, unity and permanent neutrality need a referendum (Art. 142). The template's two_thirds, the referendum tier read as optional. Constitution of Moldova, Arts. 141-143.
amendment._referendum_note: Art. 142(1)'s referendum is mandatory for the entrenched provisions only -- a split the field cannot carry. The 2024 EU-accession referendum amended the preamble by that route. Constitution of Moldova, Art. 142.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Art. 142(2) forbids revisions that suppress rights; the form of government is amendable, as the 2000 move to an indirectly elected President and the 2016 return to a direct one show.

judicial._note: A Constitutional Court reviews the constitutionality of laws (Arts. 134-140). Constitution of Moldova, Art. 135.

formation._note: The President designates a candidate after consulting the factions, and Parliament invests the government by a majority of elected deputies (Art. 98). A motion of censure carries with a majority of deputies (Art. 106), read as simple_present. Constitution of Moldova, Arts. 98, 106.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. The medieval Principality of Moldavia is the nearest crown; the restored line here is fictional.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/Ministry of Finance ~2024, rounded, on AUT.json's conventions. VAT 20% standard; corporate 12%; income 12% flat; capital gains 6% (half the gain taxed at 12%); no wealth tax. Revenue ~31% of GDP includes social contributions. Debt ~38% of GDP (end-2024). Pensions 9.5% is an ageing, emigrating population's heaviest line. Spending scaled to expenditure near 39% of GDP. The breakaway Transnistrian region is inside the territory and outside every figure here, the census and the budget's own boundary.
